title_original: Inside the Photographic Archive: The Image Centre Opens Six Research Fellowships for 2027

blocks.text: The Image Centre in Toronto invites Canadian and international scholars, researchers and artists to apply for six fellowships supporting original research across its extensive photography collections, with opportunities ranging from artistic research to postdoctoral study.
Open Call:

Applications are open for The Image Centre’s 2027 Research Fellowships, offering researchers and artists the opportunity to work directly with significant photographic collections and archives in Toronto, Canada.

Six competitive fellowships are available for 2027, accommodating applicants at different stages of academic and artistic practice. Research may draw on The Image Centre’s holdings and, where relevant, the collections of Toronto Metropolitan University Archives and Special Collections.

The opportunities include the IMC/AMC Postdoctoral Fellowship, Nadir Mohamed Postdoctoral Fellowship, Penny Rubinoff Fellowship, Elaine Ling Fellowship, Howard Tanenbaum Fellowship for Artistic Research, and Wendy Snyder MacNeil Research Fellowship.
Institutional Context:
Since 2014, the Image Centre at Toronto Metropolitan University has offered fellowships supporting photography-related research.

Its holdings include the acclaimed Black Star Collection, comprising more than a quarter-million photojournalistic prints spanning the twentieth century, alongside historic and fine art photography collections and archives devoted to photographers including Werner Wolff, Jo Spence, Wendy Snyder MacNeil, Berenice Abbott, Minna Keene, Violet Keene Perinchief and Richard Harrington.

The 2027 programme also introduces the IMC/AMC Postdoctoral Fellowship, developed with the Archive of Modern Conflict, which enables research across internationally significant photographic collections in Toronto and London.
Eligibility and Criteria:
All six fellowships are open to Canadian and international applicants, although individual eligibility requirements vary.
The IMC/AMC Postdoctoral Fellowship requires a PhD and provides a full-time, one-year research opportunity.
The Nadir Mohamed Postdoctoral Fellowship is open to applicants holding a PhD.
The Penny Rubinoff Fellowship requires a master’s degree. Current PhD students and candidates may apply, but applicants who already hold a PhD and postdoctoral researchers are not eligible.
The Elaine Ling Fellowship is intended for current master’s students and recent master’s graduates. Doctoral students, PhD holders and postdoctoral researchers are ineligible.

The Howard Tanenbaum Fellowship for Artistic Research is open to applicants at any level of education, including independent artists with relevant experience and demonstrated interests. Artists seeking to conduct artistic research within the collections are specifically encouraged to apply for this fellowship.

The Wendy Snyder MacNeil Research Fellowship is open to applicants who hold or are working towards at least an undergraduate degree and/or are photo-based artists. Research should contribute new perspectives on women photographers, including Wendy Snyder MacNeil.
Evaluation Process:

Applications are evaluated according to the clarity and strength of the proposed research plan, originality and creativity, engagement with primary sources in The Image Centre’s collections, the applicant’s ability to undertake the research, and the specificity of the proposed research outcomes.
The selection committee includes representatives from The Image Centre and Toronto Metropolitan University, alongside an external curator or scholar.

Applicants must apply for the fellowship appropriate to their research and eligibility. Blanket applications for multiple fellowships will not be considered. Previous recipients of an Image Centre Fellowship may not reapply for five years following submission of their previous final report.
Practical Information:
Funding and residency periods vary by fellowship.
IMC/AMC Postdoctoral Fellowship: $70,000 CAD annual salary plus benefits. The full-time fellowship runs from 1 July 2027 to 30 June 2028 and includes additional research funding for work in London.
Nadir Mohamed Postdoctoral Fellowship: $10,000 CAD. Research period of one to three months.
Penny Rubinoff Fellowship: $5,000 CAD. Research period of two to six weeks.
Elaine Ling Fellowship: $4,000 CAD. Research period of one to four weeks.
Howard Tanenbaum Fellowship for Artistic Research: $4,000 CAD. Research period of one to four weeks.
Wendy Snyder MacNeil Research Fellowship: $4,000 CAD. Research period of one to four weeks.

Except for the IMC/AMC Postdoctoral Fellowship, research residencies take place between 15 February and 15 December 2027 . Fellows are responsible for travel and accommodation expenses, and the fellowship stipends are intended to help offset these costs. International fellows are responsible for obtaining any required visas.
Applications and Queries:

For the Nadir Mohamed, Penny Rubinoff, Elaine Ling, Howard Tanenbaum and Wendy Snyder MacNeil Fellowships, applicants must submit a research proposal of approximately 1,000 words, a CV, a writing sample of up to 20 pages and one letter of recommendation. Artists applying for the Howard Tanenbaum Fellowship may submit a portfolio of up to ten images or film or video work of up to ten minutes instead of a writing sample.
Applications and reference letters must be received by 18 October 2026 at 11:59 p.m. EST .

Deadline: 18 October 2026, 11:59 p.m. EST Location: Toronto, Canada Programme: The Image Centre Research Fellowships 2027 Number of fellowships: Six Eligibility: Canadian and international applicants Funding: From $4,000 CAD to $70,000 CAD plus benefits, depending on fellowship Applications and general enquiries: imagecentre.research@torontomu.ca Collection enquiries: imagecentre.collects@torontomu.ca
For more information, please refer to the official website .
